title: BlueRidge Financial — Inference Cost Snapshot & Redwood Optimize Recommendations
content:
Purpose:
This working spreadsheet + writeup summarizes BlueRidge Financial's current inference economics for their customer-facing document summarization service, shows a modeled before/after using Redwood Optimize recommendations, and lists an action plan with estimated implementation effort. This is an internal consultancy deliverable for SE + Solutions to validate with the customer.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Baseline monthly inference cost (observed): $78,600
- Modeled monthly cost after Redwood Optimize recommendations: $32,900 (approx. 58% reduction)
- Primary levers: switch from single-token synchronous requests to small controlled batching, enable prefix KV cache for repeated customer docs, move production QA traffic to a 4-bit quantized variant for non-critical endpoints, and route low-latency sporadic traffic to a cheaper model with graceful fallback.
- Estimated implementation time: 3–4 weeks (engineering + rollout + monitoring).

Context and scope:
- Product: Customer doc ingestion -> extractive summarization + conversational QA (mix of sync chat and async batch jobs).
- Traffic (observed month): 1.9M inference requests; average request length 420 tokens input + 160 tokens output = 580 tokens total per request.
- Current serving model: open-llama-13b (fp16) on dedicated capacity with minimal batching (avg batch size 1.3), no prefix caching, no quantized model variants in prod.
- SLA: 95th p50 latency target 250ms for chat endpoints; many summarization jobs are asynchronous (background).

Assumptions used in the model (explicit):
- Token price proxy: baseline unit cost derived from observed monthly bill and token volume (baseline cost per 1k tokens = $0.0125).
- After-optimizations unit costs: batching improves throughput by 2.8x on average for this workload; quantized 4-bit variant reduces per-token cost by 45% for offline jobs; prefix cache hit rate conservatively estimated at 22% after implementation.
- Engineering + rollout labor cost NOT included in the cost-savings figure; only runtime/infra savings are modeled.
- Temporal window: steady-state after rollout (month-on-month), excludes one-time migration overhead.

Baseline (observed) metric breakdown (month):
- Requests: 1,900,000
- Avg tokens per request: 580
- Total tokens: 1,102,000,000 (~1.1B tokens)
- Observed bill (inference portion): $78,600
- Observed effective cost per 1k tokens: $0.0713 (note: includes infra overhead from underutilized dedicated pools)

Modeled target after Redwood Optimize recommendations (steady-state):
- Key levers modelled: batching (controlled, variable by endpoint), prefix KV caching (22% hit), model right-sizing + fallback routing, 4-bit quantization for async workers, and smarter autoscaling to reduce idle GPU time.
- Modeled throughput improvement (tokens served per GPU-hour): +2.6x overall
- Modeled effective cost per 1k tokens: $0.0298

Modeled month (after):
- Requests: 1,900,000 (unchanged)
- Avg tokens per request: 580 (unchanged)
- Total tokens: 1,102,000,000
- Modeled bill (inference portion): $32,900
- Modeled effective reduction: $45,700 per month (58% lower)

Before/After quick table (rounded):
- Baseline monthly cost: $78,600
- After-Optimize monthly cost: $32,900
- Delta monthly: -$45,700
- Annualized delta: -$548,400
- Payback on engineering effort (rough): If we assume 3 FTE-weeks at blended fully loaded cost $12k/week = $36k, payback ~ 1 month of savings.

Detailed lever analysis and notes:
1) Batching (controlled):
   - Current: avg batch size 1.3 due to chat sync constraints and naive request shaping.
   - Recommendation: implement an endpoint-level batching policy: small-window batching (20–50ms) for chat with a prioritized immediate lane for explicit low-latency tokens. For async summarization, use large sustained batches.
   - Estimated impact: reduces per-token compute overhead by ~40–55% depending on endpoint. We modeled a 2.8x effective throughput improvement across the mixed workload.
   - Risk: added 10–30ms median latency for some chat requests — acceptable under SLA when prioritized lane exists.

2) Prefix / KV caching:
   - Current: none.
   - Recommendation: enable prefix KV cache for repeated document passages and frequently re-queried contexts. BlueRidge has high content reuse (same doc chunks re-read across sessions) — we conservatively estimate 22% cache hit.
   - Estimated impact: at 22% hit, token compute saved ~22% of total tokens for those endpoints; integrated in the modeled per-token reduction.
   - Risk: cache invalidation complexity for dynamic docs (versioning) — require simple doc-version tagging in ingestion pipeline.

3) Quantization (4-bit) for async workers and QA traffic:
   - Current: fp16 only.
   - Recommendation: serve two variants — natively quantized 4-bit for background summarization and non-critical QA, keep fp16 for highest-fidelity chat sessions. Implement automatic routing by quality tags in requests.
   - Estimated impact: 40–50% per-token compute cost reduction for the quantized variant. Modeled 45% reduction for jobs that can tolerate slight quality delta.
   - Risk: small quality regressions in edge cases — include A/B monitoring and automatic rollback if eval metrics degrade > 0.5% on key QA metrics.

4) Model right-sizing & routing:
   - Recommendation: route low-complexity requests to a smaller 7B-class model with fallback to 13B on failure or low-confidence. Use Redwood's rollout and canary features to stage this change.
   - Estimated impact: reduces cost for a subset (~35%) of requests that do not need the 13B fidelity. Combined with batching, this yields additional marginal savings.
   - Risk: incorrect routing may increase hallucination risk for some customers — include conservative thresholds and human-in-loop monitoring during rollout.

5) Autoscaling and capacity commits optimization:
   - Current: dedicated pools sized for peak traffic — high idle GPU hours.
   - Recommendation: customize autoscaling policies: slightly longer scale-in grace for heavy batch windows; burst-capacity-enabled for sporadic load; recommend moving some non-sensitive workloads to a shared hosted pool where appropriate.
   - Estimated impact: reduces idle GPU cost line items; modeled as part of the 2.6x throughput improvement (increased utilization).

Sensitivity and alternative scenarios:
- Conservative adoption: lower cache hit (12%) and slower batching (1.8x throughput) => modeled monthly cost ~ $47k (40% reduction).
- Aggressive adoption: cache hit 30%, batching 3.5x, larger routing to smaller model => modeled monthly cost ~ $26k (67% reduction).
- Engineering rollback scenario: if quantized variant needs rollback and we keep batching + caching, modeled monthly cost ~ $41k (48% reduction).

Implementation plan & rough timeline (3–4 weeks):
Week 0 (planning, 2–3 working days): finalize success metrics, create canary plan, and ticketize implementation tasks.
Week 1 (engineering spike): implement endpoint-level batching and basic prefix caching prototype in staging; deploy quantized model builds for offline testing.
Week 2 (canary): rollout batching and cache to 10% traffic (non-paying dev orgs or internal), A/B monitoring, validate quality.
Week 3 (ramp): enable routing to quantized variant for async jobs; adjust autoscaling; monitor cost and quality.
Week 4 (wrap): full rollout for eligible endpoints, handoff runbooks, and cost/quality dashboarding set up in Redwood Console.

Monitoring & success metrics (required):
- Runtime: effective cost per 1k tokens, GPU utilization, median/95th latency per endpoint, batch size distribution.
- Quality: rouge-L and customer QA pass rate on sampled transcripts, regressions flagged via Redwood eval harness.
- Business: monthly inference bill delta, average time-to-first-byte for chat.

Open questions for BlueRidge TO-DO (for next sync):
- Confirm acceptable quality delta threshold for quantized 4-bit models (suggestion: accept up to 0.75% drop on key QA metric for async jobs).
- Provide representative request logs for a 48-hour peak window to refine cache hit estimation.
- Confirm which endpoints are hard-latency (must remain p95 <350ms) vs. async tolerant.

Stakeholder ask (for Solutions/Account):
- Request 2–3 hours with BlueRidge infra/ML team to collect example input/outputs and agree on quality metrics.
- Proposed pilot: 10% traffic canary on non-critical summarization endpoints for 2 weeks.

Appendix (spreadsheet-like quick calc):
Baseline unit math (rounded):
- 1.1B tokens / month; baseline cost $78,600 => $0.0713 per 1k tokens.
After: assume effective per-1k cost $0.0298 => monthly $32,900.

Notes / provenance:
- Numbers derived from BlueRidge billing export (Oct 2024) + traffic samples provided 2024-10-27.
- Modeled throughput multipliers from Redwood Optimize benchmarks for similar customers (financial docs, medium-sequence lengths).

Next steps (immediately actionable):
1) Share this doc with BlueRidge SOC/ML lead and schedule 1-hour technical alignment.
2) Create ticket OPT-321 (linked) to begin batching + cache prototype in a staging cluster.
3) Prepare quantized model build artifacts for internal eval.

Prepared by: Caleb Morris (product-optimize).
Comments and edits welcome — this is a working draft intended for alignment prior to customer-facing deliverable.
